modes.title: Late-arriving records
symptoms: Rows carry event times earlier than the rest of the batch.
Daily totals for a closed period change after the fact.
The earliest timestamp of a feed moves backwards.
common_causes: A source system replays or backfills records after the batch window closed.
A mobile or edge device uploads when it regains a connection.
A queue consumer fell behind and then caught up.

modes.title: Out-of-order events
symptoms: Event times do not follow arrival order.
A window closes before every event that belongs to it has arrived.
Sequence-dependent logic (sessionisation, running totals) gives different answers per run.
common_causes: Parallel producers or partitions deliver independently.
Retries re-send older events behind newer ones.
Clocks on the producing hosts disagree.
modes.gap: Every value is still present and in range, so no Shape check that looks at a column's statistics can see a change of order. Compare event time with arrival time in the pipeline itself.

modes.title: Timezone offset shift
symptoms: Every timestamp is a fixed number of hours earlier or later than before.
Events land on the wrong calendar day near midnight.
The newest timestamp lies in the future.
common_causes: A writer switched between local time and UTC.
A database driver or session setting changed its time zone.
Naive timestamps were converted twice.

modes.title: Daylight-saving boundary timestamps
symptoms: Many rows sit on the hour that does not exist in spring or happens twice in autumn.
Hour-of-day and day-of-week mixes change on two days a year.
common_causes: Local times were stored without an offset.
Jobs scheduled in local time run twice or not at all at the clock change.

modes.title: Encoding corruption
symptoms: Accented characters turn into two-character sequences such as a tilde-A followed by a symbol.
Text matches by value stop matching.
Email or name patterns no longer parse.
common_causes: UTF-8 text was read as Latin-1 (or the reverse).
A file lost its byte-order mark handling in a new reader.
A database collation changed.

modes.title: Unit change in the middle of a series
symptoms: A numeric column jumps by a constant factor from one point on.
Means, spreads and maxima move together.
Totals and averages look sound in each half and wrong across the join.
common_causes: A feed switched from dollars to cents, kilograms to grams, or seconds to milliseconds.
Two source systems with different units were merged.

modes.title: Column added
symptoms: A column appears that the consumers never saw.
Positional readers shift by one column.
Strict loaders reject the file.
common_causes: A source system released a schema change.
A transformation started to pass a new field through.

modes.title: Column renamed
symptoms: One column disappears and a new one appears with the same content.
Queries and joins on the old name fail or return nulls.
common_causes: A source column was renamed in a release.
A transformation changed its aliases.

modes.title: Column dropped
symptoms: A column that downstream code reads is missing.
Reports show nulls or fail.
common_causes: A source system removed a field.
A projection was narrowed.

modes.title: Column retyped
symptoms: A column changes type, for example a true or false text becomes an integer.
Comparisons and casts behave differently.
common_causes: A source system changed a column's type.
A loader inferred a different type from a new sample.

modes.title: Class-imbalance shift
symptoms: The mix of a category column moves: a rare value becomes common or the reverse.
No value is new or missing.
Models trained on the old mix degrade.
common_causes: A campaign, outage or policy change altered behaviour.
A filter upstream began to drop one class.

modes.title: Concept drift (a changed relationship between columns)
symptoms: Each column looks as before but pairs of values no longer go together, such as a city with the wrong state.
Models that rely on the relationship lose accuracy.
common_causes: A join or lookup started to attach the wrong rows.
The process that produced the data changed its rules.

modes.title: Duplicate keys
symptoms: Primary keys repeat.
Row counts grow without new business events.
Joins multiply rows.
common_causes: A job ran twice without an idempotent write.
Two sources feed one table with overlapping keys.
A merge key was chosen wrongly.

modes.title: Truncated strings
symptoms: Text values stop at a fixed length.
Emails and names lose their endings.
Pattern checks fail.
common_causes: A column was loaded into a narrower one.
A fixed-width export cut long values.

modes.title: Null flood
symptoms: A large share of a column is null where it never was.
Joins and aggregates silently drop rows.
common_causes: A source column stopped being filled.
A mapping pointed at a field that no longer exists.
A failed lookup returns null.

modes.title: Referential orphans
symptoms: Child rows point at parents that do not exist.
Inner joins lose rows; left joins show nulls.
common_causes: Parents and children load in the wrong order.
A parent was deleted or filtered out.
A key was transformed on one side only.

modes.title: Volume spike
symptoms: A table holds many times its usual rows.
Keys repeat because rows were sent again.
common_causes: A retry loop re-sent a batch.
A backfill ran against the live table.
A join fan-out multiplied rows.

modes.title: Empty load
symptoms: A table arrives with no rows although the job succeeded.
Everything that references it breaks.
common_causes: An upstream filter matched nothing.
A source outage returned an empty result.
A path or partition was wrong.

modes.title: Partial load
symptoms: A table holds far fewer rows than usual.
Parents are missing for the children that did load.
common_causes: A job was cut short by a timeout or a kill.
A page limit stopped an extract early.

modes.title: Placeholder or junk values
symptoms: Values such as N/A, TBD, 99999 or 1900-01-01 stand in for real data.
Distinct counts and top values change.
common_causes: A form requires a field the user does not have.
A default fills a failed lookup.

modes.title: New category values
symptoms: A code or status appears that no earlier batch had.
Mappings and dashboards drop or mislabel it.
common_causes: A source released a new status or product code.
A typo or a case difference created a variant.

modes.title: Gradual rise of nulls
symptoms: The share of nulls in a column grows a little each day.
No single day looks wrong.
common_causes: A field is being retired or collected less often.
A partner has started to send less complete data.

modes.title: Numeric distribution shift
symptoms: A measure keeps its shape but its centre and spread move.
Thresholds and alerts tuned to the old level misfire.
common_causes: Prices, volumes or sensor calibrations changed.
A new customer segment arrived.
